what: Open-items round, lane D: the installed two-account deployment and runtime hygiene

two_accounts.how: scripts/two_account_check.py: unshare --user --map-root-user --map-auto --mount; a private copy of /etc and an empty /var/lib; useradd/gpasswd as the installer runs them; the real deploy/install.sh --idle-access as root of the namespace; then this checkout's code as each account (setpriv --init-groups), umask 077; a fake Docker for stop and start

the state folder lets the group pass, not list
the database is readable by the group and nothing more
the resources folder is setgid and group-writable
a file that was in it is migrated
the request folder is the idle account's, for the service group, sticky
another file of the service account keeps its mode

the polkit rule names the idle account and the model units only

the idle account cannot read another file in it

the idle account cannot create a file beside it
a third account cannot enter the state folder
the idle account counts a running task while the service account has the database open
the idle pass unloads nothing while the task runs
the idle account reads a database nobody has open (no write-ahead log beside it)
what the idle account writes is the group's to read and write
the service account reads the policy's settings and events
what the service account writes is the group's to read and write
a use is marked now
a service used a moment ago stays loaded

not_shown: systemd itself: the units, PrivateUsers=yes, the path unit as a system unit
polkit acting on the installed rule

wake_start_limit.how: a transient user path unit (systemd-run --user, PathExistsGlob=<folder>/*.wake) starting `nsf resources wake` (Type=oneshot, StartLimitBurst=5 in StartLimitIntervalSec=60, standing in for the shipped 30 in 10 min), a request every 2 s for 70 s; the requests name no service, so nothing was loaded and no container was touched
wake_start_limit.shipped: --linger 25 against StartLimitBurst=30 in 10 min: at most 24 starts per window

answer_model_key_on_a_command_line.how: deploy/vllm/run.sh status with a fake docker and a fake curl that records its arguments
answer_model_key_on_a_command_line.base_793a21f: the key appeared on curl's command line once per `status` (-H "Authorization: Bearer ...")
answer_model_key_on_a_command_line.now: the key reaches curl on standard input (-K -), and only while Docker reports the container publishing 127.0.0.1:8811; otherwise it is not sent (tests/test_deployment_accounts.py)

forking_test.change: six processes started with the spawn method (race_helper.race) instead of forked from the multi-threaded test process; every assertion kept

thread_census.how: a pytest plugin recording, per test, the threads of NeuroSciFi that appeared and were still alive 3 s after the whole non-browser suite (3996 passed, 18 skipped)
thread_census.before_this_lane: 35 such threads at the forking test in an earlier census (8 nsf-voice-writer, 2 nsf-voice-follow, 6 Pocket bridges each with main, serve and upkeep, 6 nsf-pocket-setup)
thread_census.then: the voice hub fixture closes its hub; tests/conftest.py fails the session if any thread of NeuroSciFi is still alive at its end (allow-list empty)
